title: Deployment attenuation protocols — personal diary
content:
Purpose: capture a lightweight, low-friction approach for rolling out model/server changes without rigid canary traffic splits. Not a formal runbook — my scratch/diary while experimenting with attenuation windows.

Context and constraints:
- target: reduce blast radius for model weight changes / runtime flags when dedicated capacity is limited or when feature flags are risky.
- customers: mixed (hosted + dedicated). Some tenants have strict lat SLOs; others tolerate slower fallbacks.
- infra: we can route by policy, apply token-level throttles, and adjust model variant selection.

Core idea (attenuation):
- instead of binary 0/100 splits, gradually attenuate request surface area by reducing permitted concurrency/throughput for the new variant and expanding backpressure to older stable variants. Think of it like "soft canary" that levers capacity and acceptance gates rather than pure percentage.

Design knobs I tried/notes:
1) windowed concurrency cap (WCC): start with cap=10 concurrent requests across all serving pods for new variant; increase by +10 every 15m if KPIs stable. If latency or error spikes > threshold, reduce to previous cap and hold 30m.
2) token-rate attenuation: apply per-client token throughput limit (e.g., 100 tokens/min) for cohorts under test to limit cost exposure.
3) prefix-based routing: gate only users in cohort whose requests match specific prompt prefixes (cheap to implement for product experiments).
4) graceful fallback: if new variant exceeds error budget, upstream router routes new requests to pinned-stable model with preserved client session cookie.

Safety thresholds (empirical):
- p95 latency delta > +120ms over baseline for 3 consecutive windows -> rollback.
- error rate > 0.75% absolute increase OR 3x relative spike -> immediate attenuation (set cap=0 for new).
- unit-cost increase > 30% sustained across 5m -> hold and investigate.

Observability checklist (what I watch in the first 60m):
- request volume distribution (new vs stable), per-region heatmap
- p50/p95/p99 latency and tail anomalies (correlate with seq len)
- model token consumption / cost per request
- KV cache hit rate (new variant often thrashes cache)
- open file handles / GPU memory instability signals from SRE metrics

Small experiment log (notes while testing on staging):
- 2026-02-20 09:10: started WCC=10, cohort=internal-dev-team. baseline p95=140ms.
- 09:25: p95 jumped to 300ms after longer user prompts surfaced attention overhead, WCC->5 (attenuate).
- 09:40: reverted to stable: pinned-stable returned to 100% for cohort. root cause: KV cache miss pattern on first-call.
- Learn: need pre-warm priming for seqs > 1024 or use smaller context window for early cohorts.

Checklist for production flip (personal quick list):
- [ ] confirm metric dashboards have secondary alarm channels (PagerDuty + Slack alert)
- [ ] pre-run synthetic-latency suite across regions (cheap warmup set)
- [ ] create rollback PR that can be deployed in <10m (image pin + route change)
- [ ] set attenuation schedule in release notes (owner + escalation)
- [ ] notify CS for large customers in path that might be affected

Open questions / TODOs:
- what is the safe minimum WCC per variant that still produces reliable tail metrics? (need more empirical runs)
- can we automatize the attenuation ramp using simple PID control on p95? (low-effort ML ops work)
- how to map customer-tier to attenuation policy automatically (enterprise => stricter fallback)?

Rough failure modes to document formally later:
- burst-patterns causing oscillation between attenuation and expansion (need hysteresis)
- hidden correlated failures when fallback model consumes different cache keys and destabilizes downstream services
- token-cost regressions that look fine at low qps but explode at scale

Notes-to-self: keep this lightweight. Next step: run 3 more staging pushes with fixed priming set, vary WCC ramp rate (15m -> 10m -> 5m) and record p95/p99. Tag good configuration as 'attenuation-v1' and propose as an alternative to canary for small incremental model weight changes.

References and quick links (copy for PR):
- ticket: RLW-321 (safety experiment)
- last PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427
- slack thread: #deploy-announcements (search "attenuation experiment")

End diary entry. Will iterate when new staging runs finish.
